title: Windows Event log anomaly signals
description: Patterns for failed logons, audit-log clearing, unexpected service changes, and system-clock changes in Windows Event logs.

patterns.name: failed logon event
patterns.explanation: Windows Event ID 4625 records a failed logon attempt.
patterns.severityRationale: Critical because repeated or unexpected failed logons can indicate account abuse or access trouble.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Typoed passwords, service credentials, and expected authentication retries are common causes.

patterns.name: audit log cleared
patterns.explanation: Windows Event ID 1102 reports that the security audit log was cleared.
patterns.severityRationale: Critical because clearing an audit trail can remove evidence and requires immediate context.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Approved retention maintenance and lab reset procedures can intentionally clear logs.

patterns.name: unexpected service installation
patterns.explanation: Windows Event ID 7045 reports that a service was installed.
patterns.severityRationale: Warning because new services change execution persistence, but the line alone does not establish intent.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Software installs, patching, and approved agents routinely create services.

patterns.name: system time changed
patterns.explanation: Windows reported that the system clock changed.
patterns.severityRationale: Notice because time changes affect log ordering and may be entirely administrative.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: NTP corrections, daylight-saving transitions, and VM resume events are common causes.
